clue.text: Old lock fools will have shifted back to front

indicators.text: will have shifted back to front
indicators.note: moving the rear letter round to the front is a rotation of the word, not a full rearrangement

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: Some old-fashioned fools have swapped a lock's mechanism round the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The last S of ASSES moves to the front to give SASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sasse is an obsolete word for a canal or river lock, a sluice with gates.

clue.text: It shows minor change in weather; see Rosie cope with hat, going out

definitions.text: It shows minor change in weather

indicators.note: going out suggests things put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather-watcher tells us to look at Rosie managing with her hat as she heads outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An aethrioscope is a meteorological instrument that measures small temperature changes caused by the state of the sky.

clue.text: Its flowers never fade, I see, in the country

indicators.note: in places the pair of letters inside the word for a country

parts.note: a state is a country
taken as written
the letter C sounds like see

explanation.surface: Someone observes that this nation's blooms last for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: IC goes inside STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Statice, or sea lavender, is an everlasting plant whose papery flowers keep their colour when dried.

clue.text: Army or navy in its natural element

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the following word

parts.note: a navy's natural element is the sea
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A question of whether the army or the navy belongs in its own domain.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside SEA. 'Army or navy' reads as a pair, but only Army is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sena is the Hindi word for an army, used in Indian English and given in Chambers.

clue.text: Unstable left embracing Conservative

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within one's arms

parts.note: left as in went out
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A volatile left-winger hugging a Tory, in an unlikely political image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the political wing but means departed; C goes inside EXITED.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics an excited atom or state is at higher energy and so unstable, tending to decay.

clue.text: Poet's cause to bear clumsy poem with grin, lacking love

indicators.note: something clumsy is awkwardly put together, so these letters are reworked
lacking means without, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet's motive for putting up with an awkward smiling verse with no love in it.
explanation.walkthrough: POEM loses its O, then PEM with GRIN is rearranged. 'Poet's' signals a literary word: Milton used impregn.
explanation.definitionFit: Impregn is a poetic form of impregnate, to make pregnant, that is to cause to bear offspring.

clue.text: Rodent involved with making hole in wall as of old

indicators.note: making a hole in something lets another piece be pushed inside it

parts.note: mure is an archaic word for a wall
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mouse or rat busily gnawing a hole through an old wall.
explanation.walkthrough: IN pierces MURE to give MUR-IN-E. Rodent is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Murine means relating to mice and their kin, so it serves as an adjective meaning of a rodent.

clue.text: Part to south of Portugal that's popular

indicators.note: in a down entry, being to the south means sitting lower down, so the second piece goes underneath

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A region south of Portugal said to be a hit with visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, to south of means placed below, so ROLE sits under P.
explanation.definitionFit: Prole is short for proletarian, of the common people, which is an old sense of popular.

clue.text: Title of member of clergy I have come to

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend
I've, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A vicar proudly announces that his title has finally arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, which is what reviving means intransitively.

clue.text: Grating, adorned, see, I love relaxing inside

indicators.note: inside places the group within the word for adorned

parts.note: graced means adorned
v is short for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a decorated room abrasive, yet says they love unwinding indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: V plus a rearranged I LOVE sits inside GRACED.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravel-voiced person speaks with a rough harsh rasp, which is a grating sound.

clue.text: Fame not unknown to surround most of ruling party?

indicators.note: to surround means to go around the outside of the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the Conservatives, in government in Britain when this appeared

explanation.surface: Whether the governing party is famous or anonymous, asked as a political quip.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruling party is the Tories, the British Conservatives, in government when this appeared; the clipped name sits inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame of an unfavourable kind, being widely known for something bad.

clue.text: Soak English tux, shabby, then comb, given dry-cleaning treatment?

indicators.note: shabby means worn and out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp
E is the abbreviation for English
a rearrangement of the word
red, or redd, is a dialect word meaning to comb out or tidy

explanation.surface: Instructions for rescuing a scruffy English dinner jacket: soak it, comb it, send it to the cleaners.
explanation.definitionFit: Retextured fabric has had its body restored by a finishing process, as offered by dry cleaners; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Spring maybe eclipsed by winter months

indicators.note: eclipsed by means obscured by, so the word lies concealed within the next words

parts.note: the letters across the word gap

explanation.surface: Spring overshadowed by the long cold months of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is one school or university term.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring term is one division of the academic year, so spring is an example of a term.

clue.text: What's assumed in address? In this is example

indicators.note: the clue says In plus this is the longer word, so this is that word with In taken off

parts.note: an instance is an example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what is taken for granted in a speech, offered as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In this is example' means IN followed by the answer makes a word for example, so the answer is INSTANCE without IN. Address is the golfer's position over the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, addressing the ball means taking up one's stance, the posture a player adopts before striking.

clue.text: The old aim for vehicle operated remotely to partake of? (6, two words)

parts.note: ROV is the standard abbreviation for remotely operated vehicle
to partake of food is to eat it

explanation.surface: An old question of what a remote-controlled machine should go for when it eats.
explanation.definitionFit: In old archery, to rove at was to shoot at a chosen random mark, so to take aim at it.

clue.text: Amuse-bouche, favourite I used as filling for stewed pears

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so this pair sits within the fruit
stewed fruit breaks down and loses its shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
a rearrangement of the word
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A chef describes a pre-dinner nibble: stewed pears filled with a favourite ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: An amuse-bouche is a small savoury served before a meal to stimulate the palate, an appetiser.

clue.text: Piece of outstanding Italian art? Cheers (loudly) about position

indicators.note: about means around, so the cry goes round the other word

parts.note: rivo is an old shouted drinking cry, found in Shakespeare
the lie of something is its position

explanation.surface: A toast loudly raised over a fine Italian artwork and its placement.
explanation.walkthrough: '(loudly)' only says the cry is shouted, as drinkers' cries are; nothing is spoken for its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rilievo is Italian for relief sculpture, whose figures literally stand out from the background, hence outstanding.

clue.text: Pat of butter runs in liquid measure

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the measure

parts.note: a pint is a liquid measure
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Butter melts and runs in a measuring jug of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A print of butter is a moulded block stamped with a decorative design, a dairy term.

clue.text: Sailor's slack shift

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nautical verb, to pay out or let out a rope

explanation.surface: A lazy sailor's work period.
explanation.walkthrough: Slack looks like a noun or adjective about idleness, and shift like a work period; both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors veer a cable by letting it run out, and the wind veers when it changes direction.

clue.text: Small fish, one nibbling on end of simple line

parts.note: one who picks at food nibbles

indicators.note: end of keeps only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of the word
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An angler's picture of a little fish nibbling the bait on a plain line.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickerel is a young or small pike, or one of several small North American pike species.

clue.text: Monitor? Pin gold up on one

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an means one

explanation.surface: A supervisor pins up a gold medal on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' suggests a screen or overseer; it is the lizard. On means placed above in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The leguaan is a large South African monitor lizard; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Help I needed cutting a caper?

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the letter goes into the phrase

parts.note: a caper is a dance, a playful skip
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls needing assistance to perform a leaping dance step.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidance is an old word for assistance or aid, hence help.

clue.text: Boy nets fish caught laterally

indicators.note: to net something is to trap it inside a mesh
caught repeats that the fish is held inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A lad lands a fish, hooked sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-on means from or towards the side, which is what laterally means.

clue.text: Scrubbing return of TV in nightclub

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the club

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: tele is short for television

explanation.surface: Television making a comeback in a nightclub, now being cleaned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubbing means cancelling, not cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Deletive means serving to delete or strike out, which is scrubbing in the sense of cancelling.

clue.text: See west-country river infuse from below

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon in south-west England

indicators.note: in a down entry, from below means the word reads upwards

parts.note: to ret is to soak or steep

explanation.surface: A tourist told to view a West Country river soaking up from its bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, so a see in the ecclesiastical sense.

clue.text: Some Ghanaians appearing in sweatshirts

indicators.note: appearing in means found inside the next word

parts.note: letters from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A group of Ghanaian people turning up dressed in sweatshirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tshi, or Twi, are an Akan people of Ghana, and their language bears the same name.

clue.text: Grass: it's coming up in spring

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grass that sprouts in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a water source. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipa is a genus of feather grasses, so the answer names a kind of grass.

clue.text: Rock that's dark-coloured with a hint of red in

indicators.note: with followed by in at the end says the letter is put inside

parts.note: sad is an old word for dull or dark in colour

indicators.note: a hint is a small trace, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dark stone with a reddish tinge running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sard is a reddish-brown variety of chalcedony, a mineral, so loosely a rock.

clue.text: One endlessly waited for party having learnt about it

indicators.note: about it means wrapped around the thing just named

parts.note: to have got something is to have learnt it, as in got it by heart
a do is a party

explanation.walkthrough: 'One endlessly waited for' reads like a lover or a bus, but is a famous stage character.
explanation.definitionFit: In Beckett's play Waiting for Godot, the title character never arrives while the tramps wait endlessly.

clue.text: Refreshing drink making a change to ace diet (7, two words)

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cooling beverage that improves an otherwise excellent diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is chilled tea served with ice, a popular cold beverage on hot days.

clue.text: Part of an erg, directly divisible by unit of measurement

clue.text: Has (briefly) death-notice around life's end provided as once

parts.note: obit is short for obituary

indicators.note: end keeps only the final letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An obituary that briefly sums up how a life ended.

clue.text: Lewdness free? Aged, released from that, cheer about it

indicators.note: about it means wrapped around what remains

parts.note: rah is a cheer

parts.note: uncaged means set free
taken as written

clue.text: Earned endless pence with cord all tight? This performer might have (10, two words)

parts.note: the word with its last letter gone

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on the wordplay: a tightrope performer might well have a cord pulled tight.

clue.text: One rarely holds whip to improve defence in being surrounded

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The rein arm is the rider's arm that holds the reins, so it is not the one carrying the whip.

clue.text: Penniless, deny having to work, retaining energy

indicators.note: retaining means holding something within

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A broke person refuses to get a job while keeping their energy up.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means poor and in want, lacking money, so penniless.
